decisive_items: a 10-year history of a right‐sided scalp mass that had been stable and nontender until it was excised
the lesion recurred, gradually enlarged, ulcerated, and bled easily
a multilobulated, hyperdense, ulcerative right frontal scalp lesion
response.rationale: The long-standing stable scalp mass, recurrence after excision, and African-origin demographic strongly favor dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans; later ulceration and metastases suggest fibrosarcomatous transformation. Squamous cell carcinoma is the closest alternative because of the fungating/bleeding scalp mass with nodal and bone metastases, but it lacks the prolonged pre-excision stable phase.

rejected.why: Fungating bleeding scalp tumor with metastases fits angiosarcoma, but the 10-year stable pre-excision phase and demographic are atypical.
Reasonable runner-up for fungating ulcerative scalp carcinoma with nodal and bone metastases, but less consistent with the long stable mass and recurrence after excision.
Multiple skin lesions and lymphadenopathy are nonspecific; no 10-year stable mass/recurrence pattern or systemic lymphoma features.
Aggressive cutaneous tumor with nodal and bone metastases, but the 10-year stable history and African origin are atypical for Merkel cell carcinoma.
Initial stable mass could suggest basal cell carcinoma, but bleeding, ulceration, and distant metastases are highly atypical.
Metastatic disease is a staging descriptor rather than a primary diagnosis; the scalp lesion is the primary process.
